title: A Lament for the Princes of Israel

questions.question: What is Ezekiel commanded to raise up for the princes of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:1 (ESV): "And you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,"

questions.question: In the first part of the lament, what animal is the mother of the princes compared to?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:2 (ESV): "and say: What was your mother? A lioness! Among lions she crouched; in the midst of young lions she reared her cubs."

questions.question: What did the first young lion (Jehoahaz) learn to do?
options: He learned to catch prey; he devoured men
He learned to roar; he terrified the beasts
He learned to hide in the thicket
He learned to fight the older lions
questions.correctAnswer: He learned to catch prey; he devoured men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:3 (ESV): "And she brought up one of her cubs; he became a young lion, and he learned to catch prey; he devoured men."

questions.question: What happened to this first young lion when the nations sounded an alarm against him?
options: He was caught in their pit, and they brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt
He was shot by archers and died
He was starved in a cage in Babylon
He fled to the mountains and perished
questions.correctAnswer: He was caught in their pit, and they brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:4 (ESV): "The nations heard about him; he was caught in their pit, and they brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt." (Jehoahaz was taken captive to Egypt by Pharaoh Neco).

questions.question: When the mother saw that her hope was lost, what did she do?
options: She took another of her cubs and made him a young lion
questions.correctAnswer: She took another of her cubs and made him a young lion
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:5 (ESV): "When she saw that she waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion."

questions.question: What did this second young lion (Jehoiachin/Zedekiah) do as he prowled among the lions?
options: He learned to catch prey; he devoured men, and he ravaged their strongholds and laid waste their cities
He submitted to the king of Babylon
He made peace with the surrounding nations
He built a great wall around his den
questions.correctAnswer: He learned to catch prey; he devoured men, and he ravaged their strongholds and laid waste their cities
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:6-7 (ESV): "He prowled among the lions; he became a young lion, and he learned to catch prey; he devoured men. And he ravaged their strongholds, and laid waste their cities..."

questions.question: How did the nations capture this second young lion?
options: They spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit
They trapped him with a piece of meat
They burned his den with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:8 (ESV): "Then the nations set against him from provinces on every side; they spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit."

questions.question: Where was this second young lion brought in a cage?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:9 (ESV): "With hooks they put him in a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon;"

questions.question: Why was the lion brought into a net and taken to the strongholds?
options: That his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel
So that he could entertain the king
To serve as a warning to other animals
questions.correctAnswer: That his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:9 (ESV): "they brought him into strongholds, that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel."

questions.question: In the second part of the lament, what is the mother compared to?
options: A vine in a vineyard planted by the water
A fig tree planted in rocky soil
An olive tree blooming in the sun
questions.correctAnswer: A vine in a vineyard planted by the water
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:10 (ESV): "Your mother was like a vine in a vineyard planted by the water, fruitful and full of branches by reason of abundant water,"

questions.question: What did the vine use its strong stems for?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:11 (ESV): "and its strong stems became rulers' scepters;"

questions.question: What happened to the vine in fury?
options: The vine was plucked up in fury, cast down to the ground
It was pruned by the gardener
The fruit was stolen by foxes
It was drowned in a flood
questions.correctAnswer: The vine was plucked up in fury, cast down to the ground
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:12 (ESV): "But the vine was plucked up in fury, cast down to the ground;"

questions.question: What destroyed the fruit of the vine and dried it up?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:12 (ESV): "the east wind dried it up; its fruit was stripped off, its strong stem was withered; the fire consumed it."

questions.question: Where is the transplanted vine now planted?
options: In the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land
In the king's garden in Babylon
Back on the mountains of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: In the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:13 (ESV): "Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land."

questions.question: What broke out from the stem of its shoots and consumed its fruit, so that there remains in it no strong stem, no scepter for ruling?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 19:14 (ESV): "And fire has gone out from the stem of its shoots, has consumed its fruit, so that there remains in it no strong stem, no scepter for ruling."

key_verse_text: "And fire has gone out from the stem of its shoots, has consumed its fruit, so that there remains in it no strong stem, no scepter for ruling. This is a lamentation and has become a lamentation."
